text.p: September notionnel futures on MATIF are due for a pullback, but the market is likely to ignore the signals and press ahead, technical analysts said on Tuesday.
"The market is very overstretched and should see some consolidation, but it is in a very powerful uptrend," said David Sneddon, technical analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston in London.
The notionnel contract has a resistance zone between 130.52 and 130.78, which Sneddon said was a combination of price and retracement levels.
It was trading at 130.52 at 0751 GMT, unchanged from Monday's settlement price and 10 basis points below the contract high.
Hans Guenter Redeker, technical analyst at Chase in London, put resistance at 130.76, the May high on continuation charts set on May 16.
Initial support for the contract is at 130.38, an area of price action, Sneddon said.
Below there, 130.14 provides strong support, he added.
Daily continuation charts show the contract reached a high of 130.14 on May 21, gapped up at the open to 130.16 on June 13, and peaked at 130.16 on July 4.
"While the contract is above 130.14 we will continue to look for a break of 130.78," said Sneddon.
"Any corrective pullback following yesterday's strong advance will find support at 130.16 with up trendline support currently at 129.90 ahead of the 129.86 peak," he said in a research note.
The next major resistance area is 131.24, Sneddon said, the high on daily continuation charts reached on June 16.
September Pibor futures were at 96.60 at 0816 GMT, one basis point above Monday's settlement price.
